test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Panjnad is the name given to the five rivers of Punjab, namely the Satluj, the Beas, the Ravi, the Chenab and the Jhelum. It finally discharges into which sea?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arabian Sea.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arabian Sea:-**

 
 
• **The Arabian Sea, a vast body of water covering approximately 3,862,000 square kilometers (1,491,000 square miles).**
 
• It is a significant region of the northern Indian Ocean.
 
• **It is bounded by the Arabian Peninsula on the west, the Horn of Africa and the Gulf of Aden on the southwest, Iran and Pakistan on the north, India on the east, and the Laccadive Sea and the Maldives on the southeast.**
 
• The Arabian Sea plays a crucial role in the region's climate, economy, and biodiversity.
 
• **The Panjnad River, formed by the confluence of the five rivers of Punjab, ultimately discharges into the Arabian Sea.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Caspian Sea:-**

 
 
• The Caspian Sea is an endorheic lake, or a lake with no natural outlet to the ocean, located between Europe and Asia.
 
• It is the largest inland body of water in the world, with a surface area of 371,000 square kilometers (143,000 square miles).
 
• The Caspian Sea is bordered by Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, Turkmenistan, and Kazakhstan.
 
 
 
• **Andaman Sea:-**
 
 
• The Andaman Sea is a marginal sea of the northeastern Indian Ocean, bounded by the coastlines of Myanmar and Thailand along the Gulf of Martaban and the western side of the Malay Peninsula, and separated from the Bay of Bengal by the Great Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• It has an area of 797,000 square kilometers (308,000 square miles), with an average depth of 4,700 meters (15,400 feet).
 
 
 
• **Red Sea:-**
 
 
• The Red Sea is a narrow elongated basin of the Indian Ocean, extending northeastward from the Gulf of Aden at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula to the Suez Canal at the head of the Gulf of Suez.
 
• It has an area of 458,000 square kilometers (177,000 square miles), with an average depth of 200 meters (660 feet) and a maximum depth of 2,520 meters (8,268 feet).
